name: Entropy Overload applies a 20% snare-resistance aura natively (#572)
contract: Spell.dbc gives Entropy Overload 706084 a single self-targeted APPLY_AURA effect: aura 117 SPELL_AURA_MOD_MECHANIC_RESISTANCE, EffectMiscValue 11 (MECHANIC_SNARE), EffectBasePoints 19 with DieSides 1 -> 20. The tooltip reads 'Increases your chance to resist movement slowing effects by 20%'. The aura type has a real consumer: Unit::GetMechanicResistChance walks the incoming spell's effect mechanics and takes GetTotalAuraModifierByMiscValue(SPELL_AURA_MOD_MECHANIC_RESISTANCE, mechanic); both Unit::MeleeSpellHitResult and Unit::MagicSpellHitResult add it to the miss roll as SPELL_MISS_RESIST. No script or SQL is needed; this is a regression scenario for behaviour that already works. COVERAGE LIMIT: this scenario proves the DATA half only - that the passive applies and that its mechanic-resistance amount is 20. The resistance roll itself is victim-side and consumed inside Unit::M{elee,agic}SpellHitResult; the harness exposes no victim mechanic-resist or miss-outcome metric (spell_hit_chance reads the ATTACKER's modifiers), so the 20% resist rate is NOT asserted here. Proving it needs either a new mechanic_resist_chance metric in CoAGameplayTest.cpp or a statistical Ghost e2e test in which a hostile actor repeatedly casts a MECHANIC_SNARE spell at the talented Chronomancer.

steps.label: Let spawn AI and level scaling settle
No Entropy Overload aura before the passive is learned
Learning the passive applies its aura
Snare mechanic resistance resolves to 20 (data only, see contract)
